sources: THURSDAY Sep 24 2026 RUN (pre-market, 02:20 ET). HEADLINE: Wednesday's risk-off reversed Tuesday's calm. A hot S&P Global US composite PMI (fastest private-sector expansion in five years) repriced Fed expectations toward another hike - odds of an October increase moved to roughly 70 pct from 55 pct - and Treasuries sold off hard: the 10y CBOE yield proxy jumped 2.94 pct to 5.11. RATES VOL SPIKE: MOVE 95.45 at the Sep 23 close, +16.89 points or +21.5 pct in a single session from 78.56 (Yahoo Finance ^MOVE). This is the single largest one-day jump in the series this year and is the most important change in this run - equity vol barely noticed (VIX 15.18, +6.8 pct from 14.21, Yahoo Sep 23 close) while bond vol exploded. Treat the exact MOVE level as MEDIUM confidence pending a second vendor print. 2s10s 0.26 (FRED T10Y2Y, Sep 23), up from 0.25 - a second day of modest steepening away from the 2026 flat, but driven by the long end selling off rather than the front end easing, which is the wrong kind of steepening. 5y5y breakevens 2.36 (FRED T5YIFR, Sep 23), up from 2.34, consistent with the inflation-scare narrative. Brent 103.11 (TradingEconomics, Thu), up from 98.61 and back above 100 after Iranian President Pezeshkian told the UN General Assembly Tehran will not bow to threats and will not allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions stand - the diplomatic de-escalation trade that took Brent from 130.80 on Sep 15 to sub-100 on Sep 22 has partially unwound. NOTE: FRED DCOILBRENTEU printed 114.89 for Sep 22, irreconcilable with the futures curve near 101-103; the EIA spot series appears stale or backfilled and the futures quote is used here, as in prior runs. DXY 101.08 (TradingEconomics, Thu), up from 100.54, near a two-month high on the same hawkish repricing. Copper 6.6848 USD/lb (off a record high) over gold 4,281.87 USD/oz gives copper/gold 1.56, down from 1.57 - the pro-cyclical impulse stalled. HY OAS 268bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, Sep 22) unchanged: credit has not yet blinked at the rates move. NFCI -0.56 (FRED, week ending Sep 18, fresh print this run after last week's retrieval failure), still the loosest of the cycle. BDTI DATA FLAG: carried at 4,899 for a FOURTH consecutive run. No dated Baltic print could be retrieved; MacroMicro is behind a bot check and vendor levels remain irreconcilable (Investing.com approx 1,107). LOW CONFIDENCE on the level. CARRIED with no new releases: initial claims 196k (week ending Sep 12 - the Sep 24 print lands 08:30 ET, after this run, consensus 201k), building permits 1,394k (August - September figure also due 08:30 ET today, consensus 1.394M vs 1.433M prior), ISM manufacturing 54.6 (August, next Oct 1), UMich 47.8 (September preliminary, confirmed: -3.9 points m/m, below the 1st percentile of the series' history, year-ahead inflation expectations 4.6 pct; final Sep 25), LEI y/y approx -0.7 pct (August LEI fell 0.1 pct to 99.5, first monthly decline since March, with consumer expectations and building permits the main drags), Sahm rule -0.07 (August, next Oct 2), SOFR-OIS 0bp and EUR/USD 3M xccy basis -10bp (standing assumptions, no free live source), global liquidity 1 (stable, though a hiking Fed argues for a move toward 0 if tightening persists). PICTURE: this is the first run in weeks where risk indicators moved materially the WRONG way together - oil back over 100, dollar at a two-month high, both vol gauges up, breakevens up - all driven by one hawkish data surprise. The structural soft spots are unchanged and still domestic: UMich near record lows, LEI negative y/y, permits falling. The new risk is a policy-error setup: the Fed tightening into a consumer that has already rolled over. WATCH: claims and permits at 08:30 ET today, UMich final September (Sep 25), whether MOVE holds above 90 or mean-reverts (a sustained break above 130 would flip that indicator amber), ISM (Oct 1), and whether HY spreads start to follow rates vol.
